questions.stem: Let the function $g : (-\infty, \infty) \rightarrow \left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ be given by $g(u) = 2\tan^{-1}(e^u) - \frac{\pi}{2}$. Then, $g$ is -

options.text: even and is strictly increasing in $(0, \infty)$
odd and is strictly decreasing in $(-\infty, \infty)$

options.alt: odd and is strictly increasing in $(-\infty, \infty)$
neither even nor odd, but is strictly increasing in $(-\infty, \infty)$

questions.solution: $g(-u) = 2\cot^{-1}(e^u) - \frac{\pi}{2} = -g(u)$, so g is odd; $g'(u) = \dfrac{2e^u}{1 + e^{2u}} > 0$, so strictly increasing.
